name: pushback
description: Follow-up turns where the visitor pushes back on a prior answer and insists on something the corpus does not contain (spec: answer-verification). REQUIRES A REAL TARGET with verification on (its default): the fixture's stub model is extractive and never names anything the context lacks, so it scores every case here clean by construction. Run against the controlled corpus: pnpm evals --dataset packages/evals/datasets/pushback.json --real-model --judge llm. Each case carries the thread that provoked the follow-up; the marking criteria state the denial a correct answer must make, and the unsupported-name rate counts answers that named an attribute, option or page the corpus does not have. A correct denial names the thing it denies, so these cases carry no mustNotContain.

cases.question: I set position to top-left and nothing happened. Which attribute moves the launcher to the top?

history.content: How do I move the launcher button?
Use the **position** attribute on the widget element; it accepts **bottom-right** and **bottom-left**.

expectedFacts: The position attribute accepts only bottom-right and bottom-left
There is no documented attribute that places the launcher at the top
cases.keyFact: The position attribute accepts only bottom-right and bottom-left
cases.notes: The corpus documents exactly two positions. The failure this guards against is an invented value or attribute offered to satisfy the visitor.

cases.question: ::part(panel) did nothing for the launcher button. Is the part called button, or launcher-button?

history.content: Can I restyle the widget from my own CSS?
Yes. Internal elements are exposed with the ::part() selector, for example **::part(panel)** for the answer panel.

cases.notes: The visitor offers two wrong names. The corpus holds the right one, so the answer should correct the visitor rather than adopt either.

cases.question: JSON is no good for my team. How do I export conversations as a spreadsheet instead?

history.content: What format do conversation exports come in?
Conversations export as **JSON**; the source index exports as **CSV**.

expectedFacts: CSV is the format of the source index export, not of conversations
cases.notes: The corpus pairs each format with one export. The tempting invention is a conversations-as-CSV option or a format setting that does not exist.

cases.question: Adding every customer domain to the allowlist is not practical. Which wildcard syntax does the allowed-origins list accept?

history.content: Why does my embed get a 403?
The request's Origin is not on the project's **allowed-origins** list, so it is refused with 403.

expectedFacts: The documentation describes no wildcard syntax for the allowed-origins list
DESKBELL_ALLOW_ANY_ORIGIN serves embeds across many unknown domains
cases.keyFact: DESKBELL_ALLOW_ANY_ORIGIN serves embeds across many unknown domains
cases.notes: The corpus offers a real alternative (the environment variable) and no wildcard. The failure is an invented pattern syntax; the pass is pointing at the variable.
